mechanism_narrative: A lower Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) implies a more accommodative monetary policy, reducing the discount rate for equity valuation and increasing the probability of positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day forward returns is not statistically significant (p>0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL index value above 290 signals persistent inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly lower when CPIAUCSL > 290 compared to when it is <= 290 (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) and CPIAUCSL: when FEDFUNDS is at or below 0.5% and CPIAUCSL exceeds 290, it signals the Fed is constrained from cutting rates due to high inflation, leading to negative real rates and reduced equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
regime_hint: high inflation with constrained monetary policy
failure_condition: The negative return signal is not observed when both conditions hold (FEDFUNDS<=0.5 and CPIAUCSL>290) in more than 40% of cases (i.e., SPX 20-day returns are positive in >40% of triggered instances) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (defined by UNRATE below 3.5% and INDPRO above 100.0), the economy is overheating, leading to expectations of monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE < 3.5 and INDPRO > 100.0, SPX 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A HOUST value below 1700.0 (thousands of units) signals weak housing demand, which is a leading indicator of economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly lower when HOUST < 1700.0 compared to when it is >= 1700.0 (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A INDPRO value above 105.0 signals robust industrial production, indicating strong economic growth, which leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days due to improved corporate earnings outlook.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly higher when INDPRO > 105.0 compared to when it is <= 105.0 (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is inversely related to S&P 500 5-day forward returns: a lower FEDFUNDS rate implies a more accommodative monetary policy, reducing the discount rate for equity valuation and increasing the probability of positive returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The correlation between FEDFUNDS and 5-day forward returns is not statistically significant (p>0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A INDPRO value above 105.0 signals robust industrial production, which is a leading indicator of sustained economic expansion, causing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days (approximately one quarter).
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly higher when INDPRO > 105.0 compared to when it is <= 105.0 (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
